title: Function Analysis Schema
description: Standardized JSON format for LLM function analysis - Input and Output

input_schema.description: Format for submitting functions to LLM for analysis

file_path.description: Full path to the source file

existing_docstring.description: Existing docstring if any (may be empty)

imports.description: List of imports used by this function

output_schema.description: Format for LLM response - must match exactly

function_name.description: Name of the function (must match input)

what_it_does.description: Detailed description of WHAT the function does - high-level purpose, business logic, use cases, and why it exists. Should be 2-4 paragraphs explaining the function's role in the application.

how_it_works.description: Detailed explanation of HOW the function works - step-by-step algorithm, implementation details, data flow, control flow, and any important technical details. Should be 2-4 paragraphs explaining the mechanics.

type.description: Python type hint or inferred type

description.description: Detailed description of what this parameter represents and how it's used

constraints.description: Any constraints, validations, or expected formats

side_effects.description: List of any external dependencies, file I/O, network calls, or state modifications

dependencies.description: External dependencies (modules, classes, functions) this function relies on

type.description: Python type hint or inferred return type

description.description: Detailed description of what is returned, its structure, format, and meaning

always.description: Whether function always returns a value (False if can return None)

exceptions.description: All exceptions that may be raised

side_effects.description: Any state changes, file modifications, or external effects caused by this function

enhanced_docstring.description: Complete Google-style docstring combining all the above information in standard Python docstring format

usage_example.description: Code example showing how to use this function

notes.description: Additional important notes, warnings, or best practices

example_output.what_it_does: Calculates a cryptographic hash of a file using the specified algorithm. This function exists to provide a reliable way to generate unique identifiers for media files in the JellyRancher application, enabling integrity checks, duplicate detection, and safe file operations within Jellyfin media libraries. It is crucial for business logic involving file verification during moves, copies, or backups to ensure no corruption occurs. The function serves as a foundation for file deduplication and verification workflows.
example_output.how_it_works: The function works by initializing a hasher object with the chosen algorithm (defaulting to SHA-256 for security), then reading the file in 8KB chunks to handle large media files efficiently without loading the entire file into memory. It updates the hasher with each chunk using an iterator pattern that reads until an empty byte string is returned, ensuring all file content is processed. Finally, it formats the result as 'algorithm:hexdigest' to provide both the algorithm used and the hash value in a single string.

parameters.name: file_path
parameters.description: The path to the file to hash. Must point to an existing file that is readable.
parameters.constraints: File must exist and be readable

parameters.name: algorithm
parameters.description: The hash algorithm to use, such as 'sha256', 'md5', or 'sha1'. Defaults to 'sha256' for cryptographic strength.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid algorithm supported by hashlib

return_value.description: The hash string in the format 'algorithm:hexdigest', e.g., 'sha256:a1b2c3d4...'. This format allows both the algorithm and hash value to be preserved together.

exceptions.when: If the file at file_path does not exist
exceptions.why: The function attempts to open the file for reading, which will fail if the file doesn't exist

exceptions.when: If the specified algorithm is not supported by hashlib
exceptions.why: hashlib.new() will raise ValueError for unsupported algorithm names

example_output.enhanced_docstring:
Calculate a cryptographic hash of a file using the specified algorithm.

This function exists to provide a reliable way to generate unique identifiers
for media files in the JellyRancher application, enabling integrity checks,
duplicate detection, and safe file operations within Jellyfin media libraries.
It is crucial for business logic involving file verification during moves,
copies, or backups to ensure no corruption occurs.

The function works by initializing a hasher object with the chosen algorithm
(defaulting to SHA-256 for security), then reading the file in 8KB chunks to
handle large media files efficiently without loading the entire file into memory.
It updates the hasher with each chunk and formats the result as 'algorithm:hexdigest'.

Args:
    file_path (pathlib.Path): The path to the file to hash.
    algorithm (str, optional): The hash algorithm to use, such as 'sha256',
        'md5', or 'sha1'. Defaults to 'sha256' for cryptographic strength.

Returns:
    str: The hash string in the format 'algorithm:hexdigest', e.g.,
        'sha256:a1b2c3d4...'.

Raises:
    FileNotFoundError: If the file at file_path does not exist.
    ValueError: If the specified algorithm is not supported by hashlib.

Side Effects:
    None. The function is read-only and does not modify the file.

Example:
    >>> from pathlib import Path
    >>> hash_value = hash_file(Path('movie.mkv'))
    >>> print(hash_value)
    sha256:abc123def456...
example_output.usage_example:
from pathlib import Path
from scripts.utils.file_utils import hash_file

# Hash a media file
file_hash = hash_file(Path('movie.mkv'))
print(f'File hash: {file_hash}')

# Use different algorithm
md5_hash = hash_file(Path('movie.mkv'), algorithm='md5')
notes: Uses 8KB chunks to handle large files efficiently
SHA-256 is recommended for security-sensitive applications
The returned format includes both algorithm and hash for clarity
